title: Arkret Contact and Direct Conversation Operation DTOs
description: Closed request/response DTO bundle for the Contact lifecycle: request, respond, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, the portable basis evidence bundle, acceptance receipts and the peer Contact carrier, plus the contact-list projection.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

subject_id.description: Principal DID whose private Contact projection receives this fact.

recipient_service_id.description: Principal Server service DID that hosts subject_id and accepts this delivery.

previous_terminal_basis_id.description: Absent only for a root Contact basis. On recontact it is copied from every signed request fact and request acceptance receipt in this bundle and points to the immediately preceding terminal basis. The bundle field is derived convenience, never independent authority.

terminal.description: Signed current-head classification. true means head_event_ref is an accepted ak.contact.tombstoned terminal head for this basis; false means the basis remains non-terminal. A historical predecessor in a recontact continuity chain requires true from both directional proofs.

effective_scopes.description: Optional shorthand. When present, MUST equal bidirectional_scopes.

peer_service_id.description: Optional. Principal Server service DID hosting the peer, when known (e.g. learned from a cross-Principal-Server contact delivery). Lets the holder address responses/invites to the peer's home server. Omitted for same-Principal-Server contacts.

contact_next_prepare_input.description: Closed successor cursor for the holder's own issuer-local Contact lineage, carried only by the ak.self.contact.read.list projection. The container name carries the tense: version is the version the NEXT Event carries, that is current head version plus one, hence the minimum of 2; predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head Event ID, that is the predecessor the next Event must name, and never the predecessor of the current head. The three field names are byte-identical to the prepare-phase fields of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update and ak.self.contact.command.tombstone and MUST be copied verbatim; a client MUST NOT rename, recompute or derive them, and MUST NOT assemble a successor from request_event_ref, response_event_ref or tombstone_event_ref, which are projection summaries and not authoritative lineage heads. Presence is fixed by contact_state: an accepted row MUST carry it, and a pending_outgoing, pending_incoming, rejected, expired or tombstoned row MUST NOT, because the first two have no basis or lineage yet and the last three are terminal. Absence is the sole encoding of 'no successor is authorable now'; no extra error code or contact_state value expresses it. A stale cursor is refused by prepare with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale; the client MUST re-read this operation and retry with the fresh values, and MUST NOT guess a head or retry the same triple.

previous_terminal_basis_id.description: Immediate previously accepted terminal Contact basis for a recontact request. The Principal Server MUST require an exact local terminal-basis match when present and MUST require it when a terminal predecessor exists.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Principal Server cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

contact_prepared_event_draft.description: Service-fixed canonical Event bytes without the holder proof. The client may only append the proof; after removing that proof the commit Event must equal these bytes, ID and digest exactly.

direct_conversation_summary.description: Contact-list projection of an already materialized stable Direct Conversation. Coordinates and binding identity are immutable; state only says whether the same conversation is currently sendable. Creation progress is exposed only by direct_conversation_resolve_outcome; there is no durable creation operation, draft or reservation.

glare_concurrency_attestation.description: Source-signed evidence that the issuer had accepted both directional request receipts while neither request slot had yet been consumed by a normal response or rejection. Exactly one attestation from each pair member is required by the glare evidence bundle.

peer_contact_authoritative_mirror_receip.description: Only an accepted or duplicate mirror receipt proves that the immutable signed Contact fact is durably mirrored. A deferred receipt is never authority for proof refresh or glare finalization.

result_digest.description: H('ak.peer-contact.control-result.v1',{request_digest,result_kind,glare_concurrency_attestation?,current_proof?}) over the exact closed successful result.

peer_contact_control_receipt.description: The recipient signs every field except signature. This receipt is only for proof_refresh or glare_finalize and cannot stand in for a signed Event mirror receipt.

peer_contact_event_submit_outcome.description: Only the five signed Contact Event request kinds use this branch. The receipt event coordinates and result_kind must match the submitted Event exactly. Request/response may return a current proof; accepted or duplicate scope/tombstone must return one; reject and deferred never do.

previous_terminal_basis_id.description: Present exactly when this accepted request starts a recontact after a prior accepted basis became terminal. It MUST equal the requester-signed ak.contact.requested payload field and is covered by receipt_digest/signature. It is distinct from slot_predecessor, which is the issuer-local request-slot CAS predecessor and can also follow a rejected proposal.
